question: In the combined dataset that unifies the trees data with the income data by ZIP code, filling missing ZIP values where necessary, which three boroughs, restricted to records with median and mean income both greater than zero and a valid borough name, contain the highest number of trees, and what is the average mean income for each of these three boroughs?
sql:
-- Final answer with borough-level income filling
WITH income_trees_distinct AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT zipcode, Estimate_Median_income, Estimate_Mean_income
  FROM income_trees
),
borough_income AS (
  SELECT t.boroname, 
         AVG(1.0 * i.Estimate_Mean_income) as borough_mean_income, 
         AVG(1.0 * i.Estimate_Median_income) as borough_median_income
  FROM trees t
  JOIN income_trees_distinct i ON t.zipcode = i.zipcode
  GROUP BY t.boroname
),
combined AS (
  SELECT 
    t.boroname,
    CASE WHEN i.zipcode IS NULL THEN bi.borough_mean_income ELSE i.Estimate_Mean_income END as filled_mean_income,
    CASE WHEN i.zipcode IS NULL THEN bi.borough_median_income ELSE i.Estimate_Median_income END as filled_median_income
  FROM trees t
  LEFT JOIN income_trees_distinct i ON t.zipcode = i.zipcode
  LEFT JOIN borough_income bi ON t.boroname = bi.boroname
)
SELECT 
  boroname,
  COUNT(*) as tree_count,
  ROUND(AVG(filled_mean_income), 2) as avg_mean_income
FROM combined
WHERE filled_median_income > 0 
  AND filled_mean_income > 0 
  AND boroname IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY boroname
ORDER BY tree_count DESC
LIMIT 3
